                if isinstance(tabular_data.index.name, list):
                    keys[:0] = tabular_data.index.name

                    keys[:0] = [tabular_data.index.name]

## Summary

The bug was in `_format_table` in `tabulate/__init__.py`. A `SEPARATING_LINE` is the sentinel string `"\001"`, but it was being passed through `_pad_row`, which iterates strings char-by-char and corrupted it into `[" \001 "]`. The later `_is_separating_line` check then failed to recognize it, so it was rendered as a data row instead of a rule.

Two fixes:

1. **`tabulate/__init__.py:2369`** — Skip padding for separating-line rows so they stay recognizable:
   ```python
   padded_rows = [row if _is_separating_line(row) else pad_row(row, pad) for row in rows]
   ```

2. **`tabulate/__init__.py:2379-2401`** — The `linebetweenrows` branch (grid, fancy_grid, heavy_grid, etc.) never checked for separating lines. It now renders them as a rule (using `fmt.linebetweenrows`), with look-ahead to avoid a duplicate line, and uses an iterator over `rowaligns` so alignment values stay correctly paired with data rows (since `rowaligns` excludes separating-line entries).

The previously-failing `test_with_padded_columns_with_sep_line` (psql) now passes, and separating lines render as rules across all formats tested (psql, grid, fancy_grid, simple, plain, heavy_grid, github, presto).
